lines.en: Hi Omar! Did you finish the research article I sent you?
Hi Sara. I did. What the data demonstrate is not that the method fails, but that its success depends on conditions we rarely meet.
That sounds like the study, the findings of which were published last year.
The very one. Not until the experiment had been repeated forty times did the journal agree to publish the results.
Forty times! I would call that thorough.
And I would call that an understatement. It would be an understatement to say the reviewers were demanding.
You are learning fast. What the reviewer called 'not entirely successful' was, by any honest measure, years of work.
It is ironic that the harshest criticism came from the professor who taught me research methods.
Speaking of emphasis, what did you think of the article's conclusion?
What the report actually says, contrary to the headlines, is that more research is needed.
It is the small print, not the promises, that decides what a study really means.
Only when you read the methods section do you see how narrow the experiment really was.
Precision matters there. What the law forbids and what the law punishes are two very different things.
True. The article states the effect appeared 'within' the first group, which is not the same as 'across' all groups.
However similar 'affect' and 'effect' may look, confusing them can change a conclusion completely.
Not until you try to translate the abstract do you discover how much meaning lives outside the words.
You know what this article really needs? A story.
What every good storyteller knows is that the ending must feel both surprising and inevitable.
It is not the events themselves that make a story, but the order in which they are revealed.
Had the paper opened with the conclusion, the reader would have understood everything too soon.
Not until the final chapter do we learn that the narrator has been hiding the real sample size all along.
Now you are joking. But it is said that every family has one story that is told at every gathering, and one that never is.
What is your family's untold story?
If I told you, it would not be untold anymore.
Fair enough. Were the story told from the villain's point of view, we might find ourselves forgiving him.
Little by little, the details fall into place, and what seemed a confusion turns out to be a design.
Like your research project, I hope.
Were the sample larger, the findings would carry considerably more weight. That is the design I need.
Then go find more participants. Rarely does a single paper change a whole field, but when it does, textbooks are rewritten.
One day, Sara. One day my name will be in one of those textbooks.
